subject: general
question:
Fill in the blank:
The Census in India is conducted every ______ years.
solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Census** in **India** is a decennial exercise, which means it is conducted every **10 years**. This regularity ensures that the government has updated **demographic**, **social**, and **economic** data to formulate effective policies.

• The responsibility of conducting the decennial **Census** rests with the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, **India**, which operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, **Government of India**.

• The legal framework for the census is provided by the **Census Act of 1948**. This act empowers the **Central Government** to take a census and makes it mandatory for citizens to answer the census questions truthfully while ensuring the **confidentiality** of the information provided.

• Historically, the first non-synchronous census in **India** was conducted in **1872** during the tenure of **Lord Mayo**. However, the first synchronous (complete and simultaneous) census was held in **1881** under **Lord Ripon**. Since **1881**, the census has been conducted uninterruptedly every **10 years**.

• The **2011 Census** marked the **15th** census of **India** since **1872** and the **7th** census since **Independence**. The other options like **5**, **15**, or **20** years are incorrect as they do not align with the statutory and historical practice of the **Indian** government.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Census 2011 Findings**: According to the **2011 Census**, the total population of **India** was **1,210,854,977** (approximately **1.21 billion**). The **literacy rate** was recorded at **74.04%**, and the **sex ratio** was **943** females per **1000** males.

• **Postponement of 2021 Census**: The **16th** Indian Census, which was scheduled to take place in **2021**, was postponed indefinitely due to the outbreak of the **COVID-19 pandemic**. This upcoming census is planned to be the first-ever **digital census**, where data will be collected through a mobile app.

• **Constitutional Status**: The **Census** is a **Union Subject** listed under **Entry 69** of the **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**. This means only the **Parliament** has the power to legislate on matters related to the census.

• **Delimitation Process**: The data collected during the census is used for the **delimitation** of constituencies for the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies** under **Article 82** and **Article 170** of the **Constitution**.

• **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC)**: In **2011**, the government also conducted the **SECC** to identify households living below the **poverty line** (**BPL**) and to collect **caste-based** data for better targeting of social welfare schemes.

**Important Points__**

• **Motto of Census 2011**: The official motto of the **2011 Census** was **'Our Census, Our Future'**. This highlights the importance of the exercise in shaping the nation's developmental trajectory.

• **Stages of Census**: The census is typically conducted in two distinct phases: the **House Listing and Housing Census** and the **Population Enumeration**. The first phase identifies the residential status and amenities, while the second phase records individual details.

• **Registrar General of India**: The post of the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner** was created in **1949**. This official is responsible for overseeing the entire process and ensuring the **accuracy** and **integrity** of the data.

• **Global Context**: **India** is one of the few countries in the world that has maintained a consistent **decennial** census record for over **140 years**, providing a massive **longitudinal dataset** for researchers and historians.
</ul
